# 3 Maccabees Chapter 6 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Alexandrinus) | **Section:** Divine Deliverance of the Jews

---

**1** In this same way, the God who watches over all things, the Father of all mercy, delivered the people of Israel from the danger they were in.

**2** Eleazar did not cease his prayer until God answered him.

**3** When the elephants that had been released against the Jews were advancing toward them and about to trample them underfoot,

**4** Ptolemy looked up and saw two glorious angels, fearful in appearance, descending from heaven, visible to all the Jews.

**5** And the Jews were filled with fear and trembling as they stood, positioned in the midst of the advancing herd, and the angels turned the elephants back against Ptolemy's own troops.

**6** So the maddened beasts, trampling and crushing, destroyed many of his soldiers and turned back against his own army.

**7** When Ptolemy saw what was happening, he was seized with great terror and trembling.

**8** He repented of his wicked plot and turned away from the evil he had intended.

**9** Meanwhile the Jews were overjoyed and full of confidence, because God had heard their prayer.

**10** They praised their holy God and their Savior, and began to celebrate and sing songs of praise.

**11** They glorified the mercy of God and praised him who had appeared to them in this way.

**12** And the king was now prepared to hear the praises of those whom he had sought to destroy.

**13** Calling together his Friends and his council, he said to them: You have all seen how greatly the Jews trust in their God, and how he has delivered them even from certain death.

**14** Tell me therefore, does any among you not acknowledge that God is watching over these people?

**15** When the king had said these things, the wiser among his Friends fell at his feet and acknowledged the power of the God of Israel, whose might had been shown to them.

**16** The king then called for Shimon the high priest and for the Jewish leaders to come before him.

**17** He said to them: Do not be afraid; be of good courage, for I have heard the prayer that you offered to your God and I have repented of my wickedness.

**18** I have been moved by the mercy of God to set you all free.

**19** You shall return to your homes and no one shall trouble or mistreat you.

**20** You will all receive letters from me addressed to the various communities, confirming that you may return in safety to your own places.

**21** He then issued letters which were dispatched to all the governors and officials throughout Egypt, ordering them to release the Jews and to treat them with due respect.

**22** And so the Jews were delivered from all their sufferings.

**23** They returned home with great gladness, singing hymns of thanksgiving to the God of Israel who had saved them.

**24** And all who had helped them during their ordeal rejoiced together with them.

**25** The king returned to his palace filled with joy and offered thanks to God.
